items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do you remember Mutt and Jack Carey, the two brothers? Yeah. [INTERVIEWEE] Mutt Carter, yeah.

ctx.x: Oh... Oh, uh... I can't think of that. Where did he live, the clarinet player? He lived, uh, up in town on, uh... Franklin. Taratoga near between, uh, Tulane Avenue and Gravia. Uh, and, and Gravia. That's out of that. Uh-huh. KASMIME. Oh, John K... John K... Oh, John... John... John... John... John... 된... 된... 된... 된... 된... 된... ! ! 된... Allen. No. And he went away this trumpet player. Yeah, yeah. He was a good trumpet player. But now, uh, this father, what you talking about on the bass, he was playing bass…
Now we had a... Now that's not the same guy as Mutt Carey. Mutt Carey. No. No. Mutt Carter. Do you remember Mutt and Jack Carey, the two brothers? Yeah.

Mutt Carter, yeah. He had his own band, but he had, John Cashman was playing with him, see. Me, I was playing with him. They had, they had two, uh, two Cashmans. John, John Cashman, John had a brother, played drum. His brother's name now. Yeah.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: Jack Carey played with him a while on the trombone. He was an old trombone player.

ctx.x: And, uh, did he have a trombone down here, Louis? Used the trombone much?

Well, uh, yes. I used to use trombone. He had, uh, uh, let's see. His fellow was supposed to be a good trombone player. Uh, Jack Carey played with him a while on the trombone. He was an old trombone player. And he had, uh, uh, a fella called Benny Raphael. That was a pre-old fella. He was a good trombone player. Benny Raphael. And, uh, that's all I know. Uh-huh. Most of them.
Did you have another guy named Louis Prevost? Prevost.
